key_insight: Three-dimensional nanosheet-based silicon spin qubits can be modeled to show that small gate-bias shifts strongly affect exchange coupling and can push two-qubit gate fidelity below the 99% fault-tolerance target.
engineering_relevance: The study highlights millivolt-scale control precision as a critical design and fabrication requirement for scalable silicon quantum processors built on nanosheet technology.
method: Run QTCAD 3D Poisson and Schrödinger solvers for nanosheet double quantum dots
Use a many-body solver to extract exchange interactions under process and bias variations
Apply QuTiP master-equation simulations to evaluate two-qubit gate fidelity and coherence effects
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that millivolt-level variations at the plunger and middle barrier gates can reduce gate fidelity below 99%, with additional 1/f charge-noise analysis via coherence time.
watch_item: Results depend on simulation assumptions and device control precision, so fabrication variability and noise could make experimental performance worse than the modeled case.
paper_title: Simulation of Two-qubit Gate Variability and Fidelity of Spin Qubits Built on Nanosheet Technology
